sentences.text: The matter was heard on appellant's side on 03.11.2025.

There was no representation on
respondent's side on that day.
To give fair opportunity, th
e matter was ordered to be listed on this day.
Heard Sri C. B. Patil, learned counsel for respondent no. 2 on this day.

2. Challenge in this appeal is the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XII,
Bellary (hereinafter be referred to as 'the Tribunal', for brevity) in MVC No.526/2013 dated 11.12.2014.
This is a claimant's appeal.
3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant sustained crush injury to NC: 2025:KHC-D:14967 HC-KAR the left foot which resulted in amputation of the left leg.
The appellant, as a plumber, was earning Rs.12,000/- per month by the date of accident.
However, the Tribunal took the notional income as Rs.4,500/- per month and awarded a very meagre sum as compensation.

Learned counsel submitted that the accident occurred in the year 2013 and for the relevant period, the High Court Legal Services Committee, Dharwad is taking the notional income as Rs.7,000/- per month and at least the said figure should have been adopted by the Tribunal.
4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that respondent No.2 paid Rs.5,000/- to the appellant for undergoing treatment and hence the same should be deducted out of the total sum which is being awarded as compensation.
5.

sentences.text: Having found justification in the submission made by learned counsel for the appellant, this Court is of the NC: 2025:KHC-D:14967 HC-KAR view that the notional income of the appellant is required to be taken as Rs.7,000/- per month.

2 accident, as per the evidence adduced, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is 18 as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation.1

sentences.text: However, the Tribunal applied multiplier 17.
The disability in respect of the whole body assessed by the Tribunal i.e., 70% needs no interference.
Therefore, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to receive towards 'loss of future earnings' is Rs.10,58,400/- (Rs.7,000 x 12 x 18 x 70%).
But, the Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.6,42,600/- only towards 'loss of future earnings'.
6. It is not in dispute that due to the injuries sustained, the appellant underwent a surgical procedure and there was amputation below knee of left lower limb.
Thus, it can safely be held that the appellant could not (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2025:KHC-D:14967 HC-KAR have been in a position to attend his normal pursuits at least for a period of eight months.
Therefore, 'loss of earnings during laid-up period' comes to Rs.56,000/- (Rs.7,000x8).
However, the Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.4,500/- only under the said head.
7. Further, the compensation that is granted towards pain and suffering, towards medical expenditure, towards attendant charges, extra nourishment and towards loss of future amenities is grossly low.

8. Therefore, this Court is of the view that the compensation which the appellant is entitled to receive, which can be termed to be just and reasonable, is as follows:
Head of Compensation Amount (Rs.) Pain and suffering 40,000.00
Medical expenditure 5,000.00
Towards food, extra nourishment, 15,000.00 conveyance and attendant charges Loss of future earnings 10,58,400.00 NC: 2025:KHC-D:14967 HC-KAR
Loss of income during laid-up 56,000.00 period Loss of amenities in life 20,000.00
Thus, by all the above discussion, it is clear that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.11,94,400/- as compensation.
10. Though learned counsel for respondent No.2 stated that a sum of Rs.5,000/- was paid to the appellant for treatment, no proof to that effect is produced.
Therefore, no deduction can be made out of the sum which the appellant is entitled to receive as compensation.

11. Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following order:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:14967 HC-KAR ii.
Compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XII, Bellary through orders in MVC No.526/2013 dated 11.12.2014 is enhanced from Rs.6,89,100/- to Rs.11,94,400/-.
iii. The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
